issue.title: Athena runs 39 duplicate copies of sase service/scheduler and every axe routine, saturating the host at load 70
issue.description:
Found on athena on 2026-09-20 while researching an unrelated Agents-tab selection-jump
bug. The machine is running 39 near-identical copies of every SASE daemon, saturating a
64-core box.

Observed process counts (`ps -eo cmd | grep -oE 'sase (service run|scheduler run|axe routine run [a-z_]+)' | sort | uniq -c`):

    39  sase service run
    39  sase scheduler run
    39  sase axe routine run waits
    39  sase axe routine run housekeeping
    39  sase axe routine run hooks
    39  sase axe routine run external_mirror
    39  sase axe routine run comments
    39  sase axe routine run checks
     1  sase axe routine run telegram

38 of each `service run` / `scheduler run` share a byte-identical command line
(`/home/bryan/.local/bin/sase ...`); the remaining one is the uv-tool shim path
(`.../uv/tools/sase/bin/sase ...`). That is ~270 redundant processes. Start times
cluster within tens of minutes of each other, so this is an ongoing respawn loop rather
than a one-time pile-up left over from a crash.

Resulting machine state:

    load average: 70.83, 64.20, 68.58   (64 cores - saturated)
    Mem: 62 GB total, 51 GB used, 11 GB available

Root cause is NOT diagnosed. Two unverified leads worth starting from: (a) whoever owns
service/scheduler ownership handover is not detecting an already-running instance before
spawning (see the related `Retire service_host` task); (b) `sase tui --restart-service`
is in the running TUI's command line on this host, so a restart path that spawns without
reaping is a candidate.

Independent impact beyond the raw load: 39 competing schedulers write agent state
concurrently, which produces continuous Agents-roster churn, and a saturated box
stretches the TUI's async refresh apply window from milliseconds into seconds. Both
materially amplify the selection-jump defect documented in the research report
referenced on this bead, though that bug reproduces independently of this one.

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

Athena is the always-on fleet hub, so this degrades every agent run on it: load average
70 on 64 cores with 11 GB RAM free leaves no headroom, and ~270 redundant processes
compete to write the same SASE state. It also amplifies the Agents-tab selection-jump
bug (roster churn plus multi-second refresh windows). Severity is operational rather
than correctness: nothing is known to be corrupted, but the host is one workload away
from thrashing.
task_type_fields.location: athena host processes: sase service run, sase scheduler run, sase axe routine run <name>
task_type_fields.repro:
## Reproduce

On athena (or any host showing the symptom):

    ssh athena "ps -eo cmd | grep -oE 'sase (service run|scheduler run|axe routine run [a-z_]+)' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn"
    ssh athena "uptime; free -g | head -2"
    # start-time clustering (confirms respawn loop vs. one-time pile-up):
    ssh athena "ps -eo etimes,lstart,cmd | grep 'sase service run' | grep -v grep | sort -n | head"

Expect one `service run` and one `scheduler run`; observed 39 of each.
